title: Latin America’s Hinge Election

Latin America’s Hinge Election

Tom Miller, Udith Sikand

Gavekal Research | 25 Sep 2026

On October 4, Brazil goes to the polls. No candidate is expected to receive more than 50% of the vote, so there is little chance of an outright winner. Instead, the incumbent left-leaning president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is likely to face off against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of barred former president Jair Bolsonaro, in the second round on October 25. Current polling has the pair statistically tied in simulated run-offs. The result may determine whether the United States maintains its extra 25% tariff on Brazil, and will have important implications for the political balance of Latin America.Whoever wins will inherit an economy that is losing steam. Monetary policy remains very tight, despite recent interest rate cuts. Both candidates are promising to control rising public debt but will struggle to get tough fiscal policies through a divided Congress. Thankfully, the economic fortunes of a big commodity exporter like Brazil are largely dictated by the global economic backdrop, which currently favors higher commodity prices (see Why Commodities Trump Politics and Scott Bessent And The Four Quadrants).
